environment: Humpback whale season wraps up strong along the South East Queensland coast with record calf sightings
Loggerhead and flatback turtles return to Queensland beaches as spring nesting season begins
science: Queensland researchers push ahead with heat tolerant coral trials to protect the Great Barrier Reef before summer
sports: Queensland NRL clubs gear up for finals footy as September finals fever grips the state
stories.overview: Record humpback whale numbers cruise past the Queensland coast to close out a bumper migration season

segments.title: The Open
segments.script: G'day and welcome to ParkSyde Bright Side, I'm Alex Mercer, and mate, it is a ripper of a Sunday out there. Spring's only a week old and it already feels like Queensland's put on its best outfit for us. Stick around, we've got whales, turtles, science and footy all coming up. And I'm Jamie, very happy to be back in the chair with you Alex. Honestly the vibe today is just good news wall to wall, which is exactly how I like my Sundays. Let's get into it. Too right. First stop, out to sea, because our humpback mates are giving Queensland one heck of a send off this year. Let's have a look.

segments.title: Green Desk
segments.script: So Alex, the humpback whale migration is winding down along the South East Queensland coast, and spotters reckon this has been one of the best calf seasons in years. Mumma whales and their bubs have been showing off just off the Gold Coast and Sunshine Coast, giving everyone on the headlands a proper show. Love that, it's basically Queensland's version of a footy grand final, except the players weigh forty tonnes and don't need a video ref. Meanwhile down on the sand, the next shift is clocking on, our turtles are back for nesting season. Exactly, loggerheads and flatbacks are hauling themselves up Queensland beaches right now to lay their eggs as spring kicks off. Volunteers up and down the coast are already out doing their beach patrols, so if you're wandering the sand at night, give the mumma turtles some space and let them get on with it.

segments.title: Science & Tomorrow
segments.script: Right, let's swap flippers for lab coats, because there's some solid science news out of Queensland too. Researchers working on the Great Barrier Reef are pushing ahead with heat tolerant coral trials, basically trying to breed coral that can handle warmer water before the worst of summer hits. Which honestly feels like exactly the kind of clever, quietly heroic work Queensland does best. It's not flashy, it's scientists in wetsuits and labs doing the unglamorous groundwork so the reef's got a fighting chance. Couldn't agree more, it's the ultimate team effort between science and nature. Speaking of teamwork, let's find out what the sky's got planned for us this week, over to Sam for the weather.

segments.title: Weather
segments.script: Cheers Alex, and g'day everyone. Spring is settling in nicely across the South East, with Brisbane looking at sunny skies and tops around the low to mid twenties through the week, just gorgeous outdoor weather. The Gold Coast and Sunshine Coast are tracking similar, warm days, cool mornings, and a light onshore breeze that's perfect for a beach walk or a spot of whale watching before the season wraps up. Out west toward Toowoomba it'll stay a touch cooler overnight, so don't packed away the jumper just yet, but by afternoon you're still in for pleasant sunshine. We might see a few high cloud bands drift through midweek, nothing to worry about, just a bit of texture in the sky for the photographers among us. And with that sunshine ramping up, the UV index is climbing fast this time of year, so slip, slop, slap becomes the golden rule again. Back to you Alex and Jamie.

segments.title: The Scoreboard
segments.script: Thanks Sam, love a forecast with a side of sunscreen advice. Now footy fans, September means one thing, finals fever, and Queensland's NRL clubs are right in the thick of it as the finals series builds momentum. It's that time of year where every suburb turns into a sea of jerseys and every pub argument is about who should've been picked. Whichever Queensland side you're barracking for, there's genuine excitement building around the state right now. Too right, and win or lose, that's the beauty of finals footy, it brings people together over a snag and a cold drink. Big weeks ahead, so get around your local team.

segments.title: Overview & Outro
segments.script: That's the Bright Side for today, whales putting on a farewell show, turtles clocking back in, scientists working hard for the reef, and footy finals heating up nicely. Honestly what a lineup, this state just doesn't do things by halves does it. Big thanks to Sam for keeping us sun smart and ready for the week ahead. Couldn't have said it better myself. If you spot a whale, a turtle track, or your team through to the next round, snap a pic and send it our way. We'd love to see it. Get outside, soak up that spring sunshine, and we'll catch you all again next time. Look after each other out there, Queensland. See ya.
